rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: HARM: rule prevents bold monoculture that erases scan value — when everything is bold, nothing is. (a) Chunk 2 'Prework' line 10: `**A real slice you'd send off rather than nudge bit by bit. Bigger than a typo-fix, smaller than an epic.**` bolds a full ~20-word narrative sentence, not a handle (no coined term/law/checklist name here) — matches the banned shape 'never a whole lead sentence' verbatim. Harm present: this is a normal narrative Prework slide, and the bolded sentence reads as the pre-2026-07-09 monoculture the rule targets. (b) Chunk 9 'Pre-reads before Module 5' (a reading-list/menu slide, confirmed via the 2026-08-13 carve-out): lines 73, 75, 77, 79 each bold the ENTIRE 'mode + title' span, e.g. line 73 `**Read, [Clean Code Is Steering: Reading Uncle Bob's Agent Experiments](...).** ` and line 79 `**Read (longer), Kieran Klaassen, [Compound Engineering: The Definitive Guide](...).** ` — the per-slide ≤1 budget is correctly off here (menu carve-out), but the ≲5-word handle cap is explicitly NOT off, and the rule names this exact shape: 'Bolding mode-plus-title is the pre-2026-07-09 monoculture wearing a list for cover.' All four entries bold well past 5 words and include the full title, contrary to 'bold the mode word alone ... and leave the title plain.' Harm present: the entry titles no longer read as plain scannable text, defeating the carve-out's stated purpose. Checked maintainer block for an existing accept-note on either passage — none found. `grep -n` confirms both loci: `10:**A real slice you'd send off...**` and `73:**Read, [Clean Code Is Steering...`.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Line 10: unbold to plain prose, or trim to a short handle if one exists. Lines 73/75/77/79: bold only the mode word (`**Read,**` / `**Watch,**`), leave the bracketed title and its link plain.
